findings.review_scope: Registered-source review of Spectral regularized kernel two-sample tests by Omar Hagrass, Bharath K. Sriperumbudur and Bing Li. The fixed 75-page PDF is arXiv:2212.09201v3, dated 1 May 2024. Numbered Section 7 (Proofs) remains main text. References end on shared page 55 above Appendix A at y=601.6620483398438; the saved page is clipped there and a separate narrow image contains only the appendix heading. No appendix body was used.
findings.inventory: Ten actual Theorem environments, in source order: 3.1, 3.2, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.6, 4.7, 4.10, 4.11 and 4.12. Complete statements were compared with rendered pages 7, 8, 12-15, 17-18 and 20-23. Theorems 4.3, 4.11 and 4.12 include their second-page continuations. Font-aware enumeration distinguishes actual headings from an ordinary-font mention of Theorem 4.11 on page 22, proof headings, Corollaries and Lemmas.
original_statements: Theorem 3.1 retains both MMD thresholds, sample comparability, the uniform source-norm hypothesis, the two constant scalings, power 1-k delta and the separate liminf non-optimality conclusion with its two alternative conditions. Its exact full-sample permutation quantile is distinct from the later reserved-sample empirical quantile.

Theorem 3.2 retains the exact finite-sample test class, minimax risk infimum, the complete inverse-decay bound and its optional bounded-eigenfunction replacement. The source inline exponent 1/2theta is not silently grouped or corrected.

Theorem 4.1 retains the full eigensystem, both centering matrices, all Gram matrices, the divided-difference matrix and all five circled terms. The printed n-dimensional vectors around A2 and the unspecified zero-eigenvalue convention remain source issues.

Theorem 4.2 retains A0-A2, both finite sample sizes, the lower and upper lambda bounds, the oracle threshold and its optional N1 sample condition. The unbound delta in that optional logarithm is retained.

Theorems 4.3 and 4.7 retain A0-A4 and B, source smoothness, sample split, qualification truncation, covariance bound, all general and optional separation inequalities, and every sample/permutation budget. Their power bounds differ, and the printed sample-size exponents involving C differ; neither is normalized to the other.

Theorems 4.6 and 4.10 retain their original sum constraint on w and tilde-w, permutation budgets and nonstrict rejection comparisons. The adaptive level result includes both occurrences of the grid cardinality.

Theorems 4.11 and 4.12 each preserve the polynomial and exponential decay cases with both bounded-eigenfunction alternatives, all eight endpoint constants, rate powers and comparison constants. Log log(N+M) multiplies the square root of log(N+M), outside the radical. Uniform smoothness hypotheses range over all theta>0, whereas the power conclusions use theta>theta_l. The kernel result retains its additional infimum, kernel-adjusted quantiles and budget, script A=log|K| and repeated alpha condition.
source_passages: All 32 source entries and ten auxiliary passages were compared with the rendered main text. The common two-sample setting, real-valued RKHS assumption, kernel embedding integrability, MMD formulas and exact/asymptotic binary test classes match pages 1-2 and 6. A0 does not add characteristicness or a Polish-space hypothesis.

The centered inclusion, its adjoint, the centered L2 operator and the RKHS covariance retain their different domains and compositions. The eigenfunctions are L2 equivalence classes with separately defined RKHS representatives divided by lambda_i. The infinite positive spectrum and optional sup-norm convention match page 6.

The source separation metric retains the half triangular-discrimination integral and its distinct Hellinger-equivalence naming context. Range-smooth alternative classes retain their original conditions without an inserted fixed source radius. Fractional powers use the main-text functional calculus; inverse powers are interpreted only on their spectral domains.

The regularizer description, functional calculus including the nullspace term, population discrepancy and covariance representations match pages 9-10. The discrepancy has a squared-norm representation, whereas the separate variational display is unsquared; both originals remain archived.

The sample split, Bernoulli-selected mixture observations, pairwise covariance estimate and regularized statistic match page 11. The inline feature difference A is archived as auxiliary A10, and the source explicitly describes conditional U-statistic status. Independent sample groups are stated across pages 16-17.

The four regularizer assumptions retain their separate numbered labels and common domain/constant context. In particular A3 is a restricted-sublevel condition with B3 and qualification xi. The two effective dimensions remain a trace and a Hilbert-Schmidt norm. Strict sample comparability B is distinct from the earlier nonstrict comparisons.

The exact and empirical permutation CDFs remain distinct; only the latter uses B sampled permutations, keeping the reserved covariance sample fixed. The dyadic grid preserves its exact power-of-two relation. The kernel-indexed alternative and joint union test preserve each kernel-specific operator and the finite family condition.
findings.dependency_review: All 82 direct uses, 159 related connections and 32 local dependency lists were reviewed. The minimax theorem does not inherit the MMD statistic or uniform source-radius restriction. Matrix and permutation level theorems do not inherit A1-A4 or power conditions; the oracle level theorem uses only A1-A2. Adaptive power theorems do not inherit effective-dimension inequalities used to prove them. The kernel-specific class does not require a pair to belong to every kernel class at once. Population discrepancy and full-enumeration regularized CDF remain saved even though no stored theorem needs them as statement prerequisites. All explanation paths follow same-paper definitions.
findings.names_and_highlights: Every natural-language title is backed by a source keyword or separately evidenced naming context. Original assumption labels and source kinds are preserved. All 32 entries have source-backed highlight selectors; any additional selector occurs in a related same-paper statement. Font checks distinguish blackboard-bold sample collections, Fraktur inclusion, script operators, bold-italic centering matrices and bold vectors. Every related theorem has a concrete path explanation.
findings.source_limitations: The 34 existing source notes remain intact, including domain and normalization inconsistencies, unbound delta, singular divided differences, matrix dimensions, nonstrict permutation quantiles and unprinted tie handling, sum-only parameter constraints, missing grid rounding, endpoint exponents, kernel singleton multiplier and unspecified uniform constants. No appendix-only definition is required to state the inventoried results after the main-text constructions are resolved. This review preserves source statements; it does not certify the proofs or repair apparent source errors.
findings.changes: Corrected Python escape corruption in eight naming-context excerpts: D8, D10, D16, D21-D24 and D30. Raw strings now preserve literal LaTeX rho, to, asymp, theta and beta commands, as checked on source pages 3, 9, 10 and 19. Four derived JSON files were regenerated; all theorem statements, original definition/assumption bodies, dependency edges and counts are unchanged. The prior JSON files, audit and extraction script are archived under review-history/before-naming-context-escape-correction/. The current audit records that correction and refreshed hashes. The per-paper rebuild uses the verified fixed PDF, needs no former temporary working files and does not create source-review status.
findings.validation: Independent inventory and census validators pass. All six regenerated content files match saved bytes. Source hash, title, author line, version, date, 75-page count, fresh clipped text on every permitted page, actual heading enumeration, continuation evidence, direct/local/recursive dependencies, naming contexts, source kinds, selectors, typography and historical artifact hashes are checked in addition to the manual review.
